title: Symphony No. 38 in D major, “Prague”
hook: The symphony Mozart took to Prague, the city that had fallen in love with his Figaro.

painting.title: The Old Town Square in Prague
painting.pairingNote: Prague’s Old Town Square, a short walk from the theatre where Figaro had made Mozart the talk of the city; the symphony carries the name of the city that first heard it.

facts: Mozart finished the symphony in Vienna on 6 December 1786. He had begun the finale earlier that year, while he was writing *The Marriage of Figaro*.

*Figaro* was a great success in Prague that winter, and a group of musicians and music lovers invited Mozart to the city. He conducted the first performance of the symphony there on 19 January 1787, at a concert the day after a performance of *Figaro*. That is how it got its name.
It has only three movements: there is no [[minuet|minuet]]. That was very unusual for a symphony in Vienna at the time, and nobody knows for certain why Mozart left it out.
The wind instruments have whole passages to themselves. Prague’s wind players were famous, but Mozart had also been writing richer wind parts in his piano concertos.
bigPicture.inOneLine: a long, grave introduction and a busy, brilliant Allegro (I), a gentle pastoral Andante with shadows (II), a quicksilver finale with the flute in the lead (III).

movements.heading: Adagio – Allegro
movements.summary: The longest slow introduction Mozart ever wrote: grand at first, then darker, in the minor, before it comes to rest on a long, expectant chord. The Allegro begins quietly, over throbbing violins, and grows into a brilliant, crowded [[sonata-form|sonata form]] movement in which many short ideas are woven together.

mainIdeas.name: The introduction
mainIdeas.description: a held D with a drumroll, solemn chords, and later a restless figure in the minor, loud and soft by turns.

mainIdeas.name: The first theme
mainIdeas.description: a quiet, smooth tune in the lower strings over throbbing, off-beat notes in the first violins (a [[syncopation|syncopation]]), answered by a short fanfare for the winds.

mainIdeas.name: The second theme
mainIdeas.description: a gentle tune in A major, then repeated in A minor with the bassoon.

notice: Listen to how many short ideas the Allegro uses, and how they are piled on top of one another. One analysis counts six separate melodies.

movements.heading: Andante
movements.summary: A gentle, singing movement in G major, in a lilting six-beat rhythm. The trumpets and drums are silent. Its calm is broken from time to time by sudden heavy chords and dark wind entries, and in the middle the music wanders through minor keys.

mainIdeas.name: The first theme
mainIdeas.description: a soft, singing tune in the strings that slides chromatically before it settles.

mainIdeas.name: The staccato figure
mainIdeas.description: short, detached notes played by all the strings together, soon climbing in the first violin.

mainIdeas.name: The second theme
mainIdeas.description: a hopeful, rising tune in the strings over a long, held bass note.

stops.hear: The staccato figure travels through the orchestra one last time, ending very softly in the bass

notice: Listen for the wind instruments in the middle of the movement. Their sudden, dissonant entries cut across the gentle strings.

movements.heading: Finale: Presto
movements.summary: A fast, light finale built on a tune of quick pick-up notes falling to a long one. Its opening recalls a hurried duet in *Figaro*, sung by two characters desperate to escape a locked room. Loud outbursts for the full orchestra alternate with quiet passages for the woodwinds alone, and the flute stands out.

mainIdeas.name: The main tune
mainIdeas.description: three quick notes leading to a long one, then a falling, off-beat line; quiet, in the violins.

mainIdeas.name: The outbursts
mainIdeas.description: the whole orchestra, with timpani, on the same figure.

mainIdeas.name: The woodwinds
mainIdeas.description: flute, oboe and bassoon playing the tune by themselves.

notice: Listen for the flute. In this movement it often stands out above the orchestra, and in the middle section it plays against the main tune.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: The Scottish Chamber Orchestra plays with natural horns and trumpets, the valveless brass of Mozart’s time, and Mackerras takes the repeats throughout, which makes the first two movements long. He had recorded the symphonies once before with the Prague Chamber Orchestra.

threads.title: Prague
threads.body: The city loved *Figaro*, invited Mozart, and heard this symphony first. The finale’s main tune recalls a duet from that opera.

threads.title: Winds
threads.body: In all three movements the woodwinds have passages to themselves, without the strings.

threads.title: Many voices
threads.body: Mozart weaves short ideas together in counterpoint in each movement, most of all in the first.
